name: Kerr-Taub-NUT Black Hole
description: Kerr's rotating black hole with a NUT parameter, the vacuum solution Marek Demiański and Ezra Newman found in 1966. It is Kerr's metric at $l = 0$ and the Taub-NUT metric at $a = 0$, it carries Misner strings along its axis, and for $|l| > |a|$ it has no curvature singularity.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit; the mass enters as the length $m = GM/c^2$, and the rotation parameter $a$ and the NUT parameter $l$ are lengths.
history: Kerr's black hole and the NUT solution came out of one manuscript [adamo2014]. In 1962 Ezra Newman, Louis Tamburino, and Theodore Unti submitted a draft holding a new vacuum solution and a theorem that ruled out a class of twisting metrics by forcing a certain constant of integration, $a$, to vanish [adamo2014]. Alfred Schild, its referee, passed the draft to Roy Kerr, and Kerr caught a sign error behind the theorem [adamo2014]. Newman, Tamburino, and Unti published the solution in 1963, the NUT metric with its twist parameter $l$, and Kerr kept the constant $a$ and built the metric of a spinning mass around it [adamo2014, nut1963, kerr1963]. So what do you get when one black hole carries both? Marek Demiański and Newman wrote it down in 1966 and called it the combined Kerr-NUT solution [manko2006, bini2003].¶Shift the radius of Schwarzschild's solution into the complex plane, $r \to r + ia\cos\theta$, and out comes Kerr's: that was Newman and Allen Janis's observation of 1965 [newman1965janis, adamo2014]. Demiański and Newman reached their solution by complex coordinate transformations too, and theirs brought in the NUT parameter along with the spin [manko2006, erbin2016]. The result is a vacuum with three constants, a mass $m$, a spin $a$, and a twist $l$ [bini2003]. Set $l = 0$ and it is Kerr's black hole, and set $a = 0$ and it is Taub-NUT [bini2003, chakraborty2018]. Brandon Carter's family of 1968, the spacetimes in which the equations of motion separate, already holds it, and Jerzy Plebański and Demiański's family of 1976 holds it too [bini2003, carter1968separable, plebanski1976, griffiths2005].¶Where did the ring go? Kerr's curvature blows up on a ring in the equatorial plane, and here the ring sits at $r = 0$, $\cos\theta = -l/a$, a circle of latitude pushed off the equator [griffiths2005]. Turn the twist up past the spin, $|l| > |a|$, and no latitude satisfies that, so the spacetime has no curvature singularity [griffiths2005, mukherjee2019]. The horizons sit at $r_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - a^2}$, so with a twist the hole can spin faster than Kerr's limit, $a = m$, and keep its horizon [bini2003, chakraborty2018]. The hole is lopsided as well: the regions where light can circle it at a fixed radius are no longer mirror images above and below the equator [grenzebach2014].¶Taub-NUT's twist makes the axis singular, a Misner string, which Charles Misner removed by making time periodic and William Bonnor took for a massless rotating rod [misner1963, bonnor1969, bordo2019, chakraborty2018]. Can Kerr's horizons and an axis free of strings share one spacetime? They cannot: James Miller proved in 1973 that for $l \neq 0$ the spheres where the horizons cross and the two halves of the axis "cannot all be covered in one manifold" [miller1973, mathgenealogymiller]. One of his two extensions covers both halves of the axis, with Misner's periodic time, and its well behaved pieces have Taub-NUT's shape, a three sphere at each $r$, $S^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ [miller1973, bini2003]. The other keeps the crossing spheres and the northern half of the axis, and Miller read it as Kerr's geometry together with "a massless source of angular momentum at $\theta = \pi$" [miller1973]. Those sources got their numbers in 2006, from Vladimir Manko, Jesús Martín, and Eduardo Ruiz: each half of the axis is a line of infinite angular momentum with a mass of its own, positive or negative [manko2006].¶Shine a wave on this black hole and it answers much as Kerr's does [bini2003]. Donato Bini, Christian Cherubini, Robert Jantzen, and Bahram Mashhoon found one master equation for fields of every spin up to gravity's, and it splits into a radial part and an angular part [bini2003]. A wave that turns with the hole comes back stronger than it went in, at the expense of the hole's rotation, and a large enough $|l|$ shuts the effect off [bini2003]. The twist is to mass what magnetic charge is to electric charge, a gravitomagnetic monopole [bini2003, chakraborty2018]. William Emond, Yu-tin Huang, Uri Kol, Nathan Moynihan, and Donal O'Connell showed that, to leading order in the strength of gravity, a duality rotation of the kind that turns electric charge into magnetic charge carries Kerr's solution into Kerr-Taub-NUT [emond2022]. The Misner strings hold part of the angular momentum, and Alvaro Ballon Bordo, Finnian Gray, Robie Hennigar, and David Kubizňák wrote a first law of thermodynamics in 2019 with a term for each string [bordo2019].¶Chandrachur Chakraborty and Sudip Bhattacharyya went looking for the twist in the sky, in GRO J1655-40, a collapsed star that draws gas from a companion and shines in X rays [chakraborty2018]. Three ways of measuring its spin from those X rays had given three answers, $a/m$ near $0.29$, between $0.65$ and $0.75$, and between $0.90$ and $0.99$ [chakraborty2018]. Allow a NUT parameter and the three agree, at $a/m$ between $2.12$ and $2.21$ and $l/m$ between $1.86$ and $1.93$, with a mass that matches an independent measurement [chakraborty2018]. Those values lie just past $a^2 = m^2 + l^2$, where the horizon disappears, and Chakraborty and Bhattacharyya called the result "the first significant observational indication of the gravitomagnetic monopole", short of a direct detection [chakraborty2018]. The hole's shadow is a second test: Arne Grenzebach, Volker Perlick, and Claus Lämmerzahl worked out its outline in 2014 for an observer anywhere outside the horizon, and found it the same however the strings are shared between the two halves of the axis [grenzebach2014].

related.text: Kerr-Taub-NUT with the twist taken out, $l = 0$. The Misner strings go with it, and the ring singularity settles back on the equator.
Kerr-Taub-NUT with the spin switched off, $a = 0$ [bini2003].
Both the spin and the twist switched off, $a = l = 0$.
Kerr's black hole with an electric charge where this one has a twist. Demiański and Newman's solutions of 1966 include the black hole that carries both [manko2006].
Kerr's black hole with a cosmological constant where this one has a twist. Both belong to the family Carter found by asking the Hamilton-Jacobi equation to separate [carter1968separable, bini2003].

A black hole with an acceleration where this one has a twist. Plebański and Demiański's family of 1976 holds spin, twist, and acceleration together, and in Jerry Griffiths and Jiří Podolský's form of it Kerr-Taub-NUT is what is left when the acceleration vanishes [plebanski1976, griffiths2005].

coordinates.name: Boyer-Lindquist

parameters.description: Geometric mass, $m = GM/c^2$, a length
Rotation parameter, a length; at $a = 0$ the metric is the Taub-NUT metric
NUT parameter, a length, the gravitomagnetic monopole moment; at $l = 0$ the metric is Kerr's
Vanishes only on the ring $r = 0$, $\cos\theta = -l/a$, which exists for $|l| \le |a|$
Its roots are the horizons, which exist for $a^2 \le m^2 + l^2$
Equal to $-2l$ on the northern half of the axis and to $2l$ on the southern half, each a Misner string

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ of Boyer and Lindquist's kind, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and a Misner string on each half of the axis, and write $\Sigma$, $\Delta$, and $\chi$ as the parameters define them. The horizons are at $r_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - a^2}$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

nonzero.value: -\dfrac{2l\,r\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)^2\cos\theta - a\,\chi^2\left(2l^2\,r + m\,r^2 - m\,a^2 - m\,l^2\right) + \chi\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)\left(4l^2\,r + 3m\,r^2 - m\,a^2 - m\,l^2\right)}{\Sigma^2\,\Delta}

-\dfrac{2l\,r\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)^2\cos\theta - a\,\chi^2\left(2l^2\,r + m\,r^2 - m\,a^2 - m\,l^2\right) + \chi\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)\left(4l^2\,r + 3m\,r^2 - m\,a^2 - m\,l^2\right)}{\Sigma^2\,\Delta}

-\dfrac{\left(\left(l + a\cos\theta\right)\Delta\,\chi^2 - \left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)\left(l\,r^2\sin^2\theta - 2l\,r^2 + a^3\sin^4\theta\cos\theta + 2a^2\,l\sin^4\theta + a^2\,l\sin^2\theta - 2a^2\,l - 4a\,l^2\cos\theta + l^3\sin^2\theta - 2l^3\right)\right)\csc\theta}{\Sigma^2}

-\dfrac{\left(\left(l + a\cos\theta\right)\Delta\,\chi^2 - \left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)\left(l\,r^2\sin^2\theta - 2l\,r^2 + a^3\sin^4\theta\cos\theta + 2a^2\,l\sin^4\theta + a^2\,l\sin^2\theta - 2a^2\,l - 4a\,l^2\cos\theta + l^3\sin^2\theta - 2l^3\right)\right)\csc\theta}{\Sigma^2}

-\dfrac{\left(\Sigma\left(\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)^2\cos\theta - 2\Delta\chi\left(l + a\cos\theta\right)\right) + a\left(l + a\cos\theta\right)\left(\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)^2\sin^2\theta - \Delta\chi^2\right)\right)\sin\theta}{\Sigma^3}

\dfrac{r\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)\left(r^2 - 2l\left(l + a\cos\theta\right) + a^2 + l^2 - 2m\,r\right) + a^2\,\chi^2\left(r - m\right) - a\,\chi\left(2r - m\right)\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)}{\Sigma^2\,\Delta}

\dfrac{r\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)\left(r^2 - 2l\left(l + a\cos\theta\right) + a^2 + l^2 - 2m\,r\right) + a^2\,\chi^2\left(r - m\right) - a\,\chi\left(2r - m\right)\left(r^2 + a^2 + l^2\right)}{\Sigma^2\,\Delta}

parameters.description: Geometric mass, $m = GM/c^2$, a length
Rotation parameter, a length; at $a = 0$ the metric is the Taub-NUT metric
NUT parameter, a length, the gravitomagnetic monopole moment; at $l = 0$ the metric is Kerr's
Vanishes only on the ring $r = 0$, $\cos\theta = -l/a$, which exists for $|l| \le |a|$
Its roots are the horizons, which exist for $a^2 \le m^2 + l^2$
Vanishes on the northern half of the axis and is $4l$ on the southern half, the one Misner string

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t_N, r, \theta, \phi)$ with $t_N = t + 2l\phi/c$, the time in which the northern half of the axis is regular and one Misner string lies along $\theta = \pi$, and write $\Sigma$, $\Delta$, and $\chi$ as the parameters define them. The horizons are at $r_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - a^2}$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct_N$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t_N}$ means $d(ct_N)/d\lambda$.

Rotation parameter, a length; at $a = 0$ the metric is the Taub-NUT metric
NUT parameter, a length, the gravitomagnetic monopole moment; at $l = 0$ the metric is Kerr's
Vanishes only on the ring $r = 0$, $\cos\theta = -l/a$, which exists for $|l| \le |a|$
Its roots are the horizons, which exist for $a^2 \le m^2 + l^2$
Vanishes on the northern half of the axis and is $4l$ on the southern half, the one Misner string

coordinates.convention: We use ingoing Kerr coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \tilde\phi)$ built on the time $t_N = t + 2l\phi/c$ in which the northern half of the axis is regular, with the advanced time $v = c\,t_N + r_*$ a length, $dr_*/dr = (r^2 + (a + l)^2)/\Delta$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$, and $d\tilde\phi = d\phi + a\,dr/\Delta$, and write $\Sigma$, $\Delta$, and $\chi$ as the parameters define them. The horizons are at $r_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - a^2}$.

domains: Q = 0 \;\text{(the horizons } q_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - a^2}\text{)}

parameters.description: Geometric mass, $m = GM/c^2$, a length
Rotation parameter, a length; at $a = 0$ the metric is the Taub-NUT metric
NUT parameter, a length, the gravitomagnetic monopole moment; at $l = 0$ the metric is Kerr's
Its roots are the horizons, which exist for $a^2 \le m^2 + l^2$
Vanishes on the axis, $p = l \pm a$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(\tau, q, p, \sigma)$ of Plebański and Demiański, with $q = r$, $p = l + a\cos\theta$, $\sigma = -\phi/a$, and $\tau = ct - (a^2 + l^2)\phi/a$ a length that stands as the time, and write $Q$ and $P$ as the parameters define them. The horizons are at $q_\pm = m \pm \sqrt{m^2 + l^2 - a^2}$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\dfrac{Q}{p^2 + q^2}\left(d\tau - p^2\,d\sigma\right)^2 + \dfrac{p^2 + q^2}{Q}dq^2 + \dfrac{p^2 + q^2}{P}dp^2 + \dfrac{P}{p^2 + q^2}\left(d\tau + q^2\,d\sigma\right)^2
